key_insight: A small tetragonal distortion in BaTiO3 nanoparticles, strengthened by covalent Ti–O bonding, can significantly boost polarization and charge retention for piezoelectric nanogenerators.
engineering_relevance: Size- and bonding-engineered, lead-free BaTiO3 offers a practical route to higher-output self-powered devices for wearable and autonomous electronics.
method: Ligand-assisted sol-gel synthesis of BaTiO3 nanoparticles
Structural verification by XRD, Raman, and PDF analysis
DFT to link Ti–O covalency with ferroelectric and piezoelectric behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~100 V open-circuit voltage and ~29 μJ stored energy for the BTO-900-PDMS device, while the BTO-1200 device reached ~649 μW cm-2 power density and ~181 μA short-circuit current.
watch_item: Performance appears sensitive to nanoparticle size, defect density, and interface control, so scaling or reproducibility may require tight process optimization.
paper_title: Small Distortions, Big Polarization: Tetragonal BaTiO3 Nanoparticles for High-Performance Piezoelectric Nanogenerators
